stem: How long has Marley been dead when the story begins?

evidence.quote: "Mr. Marley has been dead these seven years," Scrooge replied. "He died seven years ago, this very night."

explanation: Scrooge tells the charity collectors that Marley died seven years ago, on this very night.

stem: Dickens calls Scrooge "a squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous, old sinner!" What does covetous mean?

evidence.quote: a squeezing, wrenching, grasping, scraping, clutching, covetous, old sinner!

explanation: Every word around it (grasping, clutching, squeezing) is about holding on to things, so covetous means wanting more and more for yourself.

stem: What does Scrooge's answer to the men collecting for the poor show about him?
choices: He thinks the poor are not his problem
He secretly plans to give money later
He is too busy to listen to anyone
He doesn't believe poor people exist

evidence.quote: "If they would rather die," said Scrooge, "they had better do it, and decrease the surplus population."
"It's not my business," Scrooge returned.

explanation: Scrooge says the poor might as well die and that it's 'not my business.' He sees their suffering as nothing to do with him.

stem: What is the chain around Marley's ghost made of?

evidence.quote: it was made (for Scrooge observed it closely) of cash-boxes, keys, padlocks, ledgers, deeds, and heavy purses wrought in steel

explanation: The chain is built from the tools of a moneylender's business: Marley is weighed down by the greed of his life.

stem: How much does Scrooge pay his clerk, Bob Cratchit?

evidence.quote: my clerk, with fifteen shillings a week, and a wife and family, talking about a merry Christmas

explanation: Scrooge mutters that his clerk earns fifteen shillings a week and still talks about a merry Christmas.

stem: What does the Ghost of Christmas Past hold under its arm?
choices: A great extinguisher for a cap

evidence.quote: a great extinguisher for a cap, which it now held under its arm

explanation: A bright light shines from the Ghost's head, and it carries a candle extinguisher it can use as a cap. Later Scrooge uses it to snuff the Ghost out.

stem: How does old Fezziwig treat Scrooge and Dick, his apprentices, on Christmas Eve?
choices: He stops work early and throws a party
He makes them work through the night
He sends them home without pay
He forgets that it is Christmas

evidence.quote: "Yo ho, my boys!" said Fezziwig. "No more work to-night. Christmas Eve, Dick. Christmas, Ebenezer!"

explanation: Fezziwig closes up early and throws a ball. He is the kind of employer Scrooge could have become, and the opposite of how Scrooge treats Bob.

stem: Why does Belle, the young woman Scrooge was going to marry, release him from their engagement?
choices: He has come to love money more than her
She has to move to another country
He lost his job with Fezziwig

evidence.quote: "What Idol has displaced you?" he rejoined. "A golden one."

explanation: Belle says another 'idol' has taken her place: a golden one. Money has become what Scrooge loves most.

stem: When Scrooge asks if Tiny Tim will live, why does the Spirit answer with Scrooge's own words about the "surplus population"?
choices: To make Scrooge hear how cruel his words were
Because the Spirit agrees with Scrooge
To remind Scrooge to pay Bob more
Because Tiny Tim said those words first

evidence.quote: If he be like to die, he had better do it, and decrease the surplus population.
Scrooge hung his head to hear his own words quoted by the Spirit, and was overcome with penitence and grief.

explanation: Scrooge said those words about strangers in Stave One. Hearing them about a child he now cares for makes him feel their cruelty.

stem: The Spirit shows two children, Ignorance and Want, and says to beware the boy most of all. What point is Dickens making?
choices: Ignorance is the most dangerous problem a society faces
Children should be kept away from rich people
Spirits cannot be trusted with children

evidence.quote: This boy is Ignorance. This girl is Want. Beware them both, and all of their degree, but most of all beware this boy

explanation: The children belong to all of 'Man.' Dickens warns that ignoring the poor, and leaving them uneducated, leads to 'Doom.'

stem: Businessmen joke that they'll go to a man's funeral only "if a lunch is provided." Whose funeral is it?

evidence.quote: "I don't mind going if a lunch is provided," observed the gentleman with the excrescence on his nose.
read upon the stone of the neglected grave his own name, EBENEZER SCROOGE

explanation: Nobody cares about the dead man. At the end of the stave Scrooge reads his own name on the grave.

stem: What does Scrooge promise the last Spirit?
choices: To keep Christmas in his heart all year
To never speak to a ghost again
To hand his business to Bob

evidence.quote: I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.

explanation: Scrooge promises to live in the Past, Present, and Future, and keep Christmas all year, not just one day.

stem: How big is the turkey Scrooge sends to the Cratchits?
choices: Twice the size of Tiny Tim

evidence.quote: He sha'n't know who sends it. It's twice the size of Tiny Tim.

explanation: Scrooge laughs that the prize turkey is twice the size of Tiny Tim, and sends it without saying who it's from.

stem: Bob Cratchit comes in late the day after Christmas. What does Scrooge do?

evidence.quote: "and therefore I am about to raise your salary!"

explanation: Scrooge pretends to be angry, then surprises Bob by raising his salary and offering to help his family.

stem: Put these events in the order they happen.

events.text: Scrooge sees the chain Marley's ghost drags

evidence.quote: The chain he drew was clasped about his middle.

events.text: Fezziwig closes up early for a Christmas Eve party

evidence.quote: No more work to-night. Christmas Eve, Dick. Christmas, Ebenezer!

events.text: The Spirit shows Scrooge two children, Ignorance and Want

evidence.quote: This boy is Ignorance. This girl is Want.

events.text: Scrooge reads his own name on a grave

evidence.quote: read upon the stone of the neglected grave his own name, EBENEZER SCROOGE

explanation: Marley comes first, then one scene from each of the three Spirits.

stem: Put these events in the order they happen.

events.text: Belle tells Scrooge a golden idol has replaced her

evidence.quote: "What Idol has displaced you?" he rejoined. "A golden one."

events.text: The Spirit repeats Scrooge's words about the surplus population

evidence.quote: Scrooge hung his head to hear his own words quoted by the Spirit

events.text: Businessmen joke about going to a funeral for the lunch

evidence.quote: "I don't mind going if a lunch is provided," observed the gentleman

events.text: Scrooge tells Bob he is raising his salary

evidence.quote: and therefore I am about to raise your salary!

explanation: Scrooge's past, his present, the future he's warned about, and the morning he changes.
